clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the Meritorious Service Medal, with accompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of a military department or by the Secretary of Transportation with regard to the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, or by military commanders or other officers the Secretary concerned designates, to a member of the armed forces of the United States who has distinguished himself by outstanding meritorious achievement or service to the United States. Executive Order 12312 (July 2, 1981, effective on signing; the order states no later effective date) restated section 1 to permit the award also to a member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation (before: award to a member of the armed forces of the United States; after: or to a member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation). Executive Order 13286 section 61 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) further amended section 1 by striking the Secretary of Transportation and inserting the Secretary of Homeland Security. Neither amendment ends the clause, no held instrument revokes it, and the Code note still prints the order as amended, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11448 of January 16, 1969 (34 FR 915; held official text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11448.txt, read in full) establishes the Meritorious Service Medal under the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief; it has four numbered sections, which the packet inventory already separates. It cites no authority statute. Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition. Later instruments: the Office of the Federal Register note and the held-text number search show two amendments, both to section 1: Executive Order 12312 (July 2, 1981; held official text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12312.txt) and Executive Order 13286 section 61 (68 FR 10619; held official text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13286.txt, effective March 1, 2003 under section 92). Both are recorded as later events from the packet's official actor texts. The packet also lists ACT:EO:11448>EO:12977, a lead whose held source-ladder file contains the text of Executive Order 13286 and not a separate order; it adds no instrument. The held-text number search also finds the American Presidency Project copy of Executive Order 13286, the Federal Register document copy of 13286, the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification and the order's own copies; none revokes or supersedes the order. Current law: the three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR as of 2026-10-14; Office of the Federal Register catalog); the Code prints the order as a note at 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 and refers to it from other notes, and no search shows an ending. The packet carries no CURRENT record for the order, so the current predicate rests on the order's own held text read with those searches.
